s.d: ἀκρίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for אַרְבֶּה, also for חָגָב, etc. ;] a locust: [[matthew 3 4|Mat.3:4]], [[mark 1 6|Mrk.1:6]], [[revelation 9 3|Rev.9:3]], 7.† (AS)
ἀκροατήριον, -ου, τό (ἀκροάομαι, to listen) a place of audience: [[acts 25 23|Act.25:23]] (Plut.).† (AS)
ἀκροατής, οῦ, ὁ (see supr.) [in LXX: [[isaiah 3 3|Isa.3:3]] (לַחַשׁ), Sir.3:29 ;] a hearer: [[romans 2 13|Rom.2:13]], [[james 1 22|Jas.1:22, 23, 25]].† (AS)

ἀκροβυστία, -ας, ή (perh. an Alexandrian form of cl. ἀκροποσθία; cf. MM, VGT, see word) [in LXX for עׇרְלָה ;] the prepuce, foreskin (LXX), hence abstr., uncircumcision: [[acts 11 3|Act.11:3]], [[romans 2 25|Rom.2:25-27 3:30 4:10-12]], [[1-corinthians 7 18|1Co.7:18-19]], [[galatians 5 6|Gal.5:6 6:15]], [[colossians 2 13|Col.2:13 3:11]] By meton., the uncircumcised: [[romans 4 9|Rom.4:9]], [[galatians 2 7|Gal.2:7]], [[ephesians 2 11|Eph.2:11]].† (AS)

ἀκρο-γωνιαῖος, -αία, -αῖον (ἄκροι, γωνία, an angle) [in LXX: [[isaiah 28 16|Isa.28:16]] (פִּנָּה) * ;] = Attic γωνιαῖος (frequently in Inscr.; MM, VGT, see word ἀ.), at the extreme angle: ὁ ἀ., the corner foundation stone, [[ephesians 2 20|Eph.2:20]], [[1-peter 2 6|1Pe.2:6]].† (AS)

ἀκροθίνιον, -ου, τό (ἄκρος, θίς, a heap), prop., the top of a heap, hence, in pl., 1. first-fruits (Xen.; MM, VGT, see word). 2. In war, the choicest spoils (cf. Hdt., viii, 121 f.): [[hebrews 7 4|Heb.7:4.]] † (AS)

ἄκρος, -α, -ον [in LXX for קֶצַח, בֹּהֶן, etc. ;] highest, extreme; as subst., τὸ ἄ., the top, extremity: [[mark 13 27|Mrk.13:27]], [[luke 16 24|Luk.16:24]], [[hebrews 11 21|Heb.11:21]]; pl. (cf. MM, VGT, see word), [[matthew 24 31|Mat.24:31.]]† (AS)
Ἀκύλας, -ου (and -α; MM, VGT, see word), ὁ (Lat.), Aquila: [[acts 18 2|Act.18:2, 18 18:26]], [[romans 16 3|Rom.16:3]], [[1-corinthians 16 19|1Co.16:19]], [[2-timothy 4 19|2Ti.4:19]].† (AS)

ἀκυρόω, -ῶ (κῦρος, authority), [in LXX: 1Es.6:32 [[esther 6 1|Est.6:1-34]], 2Ma.6:1-31 * ;] to revoke, invalidate (MM, VGT, see word): [[matthew 15 6|Mat.15:6]], [[mark 7 13|Mrk.7:13]], [[galatians 3 17|Gal.3:17]] (Plut.).† (AS)
ἀκωλύτως adv. (κωλύω), [in Sm.: [[job 34 31|Job.34:31]] * ;] without hindrance (so frequently in legal documents; MM, VGT, see word): [[acts 28 31|Act.28:31.]]† (AS)
ἀκων (Attic contr. for ἀέκων), -ουα, -ον (ἀ- neg., ἅκων, willing), [in LXX: [[job 14 17|Job.14:17]], 2Ma.11:12 * ;] unwilling: [[1-corinthians 9 17|1Co.9:17.]]† (AS)

ἀλάβαστρον, -ου, τό (also -ος, ὁ, ἡ; colloq. and κοινή for ἀλάβαστος), [in LXX: [[2-kings 21 13|4Ki.21:13]] (צַלַּחַת)* ;] a box of alabaster (ἀλαβαστίτης) for ointment: [[matthew 26 7|Mat.26:7]], [[mark 14 3|Mrk.14:3]], [[luke 7 37|Luk.7:37]] (see DCG, i, 41b; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἀλαζονία(Rec. -εία, the earlier form), -ας, ἡ (ἀλαζών), [in LXX: Wis.5:8 17:7, 2; 4Ma.5:1-38 * ;] the character of an ἀλαζών, boastfulness, vainglory, vaunting: [[james 4 16|Jas.4:16]] (Mayor, in l), [[1-john 2 16|1Jn.2:16.]]† (AS)

ἀλαζών, -όνος, ὁ, ἡ (ἄλη, wandering) [in LXX: [[job 28 8|Job.28:8]] (שַׁחַץ) [[habakkuk 2 5|Hab.2:5]] (יָהִיר), [[proverbs 21 24|Pro.21:24]] (לוּץ)* ;] prop, a vagabond, hence, an impostor, a boaster: [[romans 1 30|Rom.1:30]], [[2-timothy 3 2|2Ti.3:2]].† SYN.: ὐβριστής, ὑπερήφανος (see Tr., Syn., § xxix; Lft., Notes, 256) (AS)

ἀλαλάζω (onomat. from the battle-cry ἀλαλά), [in LXX chiefly for רוּעַ hi., יָלַל ;] prop, to raise a war-cry, shout with triumph or joy; rarely of grief, to wail: [[mark 5 38|Mrk.5:38]] (cf. [[jeremiah 4 8|Jer.4:8]]); of a cymbal, ἀλαλάζον (RV. clanging), [[1-corinthians 13 1|1Co.13:1]] (cf. ὀλολύζω).† (AS)
ἀ-λάλητος, -ον (λαλέω), inexpressible, not to be uttered: [[romans 8 26|Rom.8:26.]]† (AS)
ἄ-λαλος, -ον (λάλος, talkative), [in LXX: [[psalms 31 18|Psa.31:18]] (אָלַם ni.) [[psalms 38 13|Psa.38:13]] (אִלֵּם)* ;] dumb, speechless: [[mark 7 37|Mrk.7:37 9:17, 25]].† (AS)

ἅλας (T, ἅλα), -ατος, τό, late form of cl. ἅλς, -ος, ὁ (MM, VGT, see word), [in LXX chiefly for מְלַח ;] salt, lit, and figuratively: [[matthew 5 13|Mat.5:13]], [[mark 9 50|Mrk.9:50]] [[luke 14 34|Luk.14:34]]; like cl. ἅλες, wit, of wisdom and grace in speech: [[colossians 4 6|Col.4:6.]]† (AS)

ἀλείφω (cf. λίπος, oil), [in LXX: [[genesis 31 13|Gen.31:13]], [[exodus 40 15|Exo.40:15]], [[numbers 3 3|Num.3:3]] (מָשַׁח), [[ezekiel 13 10|Eze.13:10]] ff. (טוּחַ), [[ruth 3 3|Rut.3:3]], [[2-samuel 12 20|2Ki.12:20 14:2]], [[2-kings 4 2|4Ki.4:2]], [[2-chronicles 28 15|2Ch.28:15]], [[micah 6 15|Mic.6:15]], Dan LXX TH [[daniel 10 3|Dan.10:3]] (סוּךְ), [[esther 2 12|Est.2:12]], Jdth.16:8 * ;] to anoint, festally or in homage: with accusative of thing(s) or of person(s), [[matthew 6 17|Mat.6:17]], [[john 12 3|Jhn.12:3]], [[mark 16 1|Mrk.16:1]]; before dative, ἐλαίῳ, [[mark 6 13|Mrk.6:13]], [[james 5 14|Jas.5:14]]; μύρῳ, [[luke 7 38|Luk.7:38, 46]], [[john 11 2|Jhn.11:2]].† SYN.: χρίω, μυρίζω (against the distinction made bet. ἀ. and χ. in Tr., Syn., § 38, see MM, VGT, see word, ἀ.) (AS)
ἀλεκτοροφωνία, -ας, ἡ (ἀλέκτωρ, φωνή), cock-crowing, i.e. the third watch in the night: [[mark 13 35|Mrk.13:35.]]† (AS)

ἀλέκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (poët. form of ἀλεκτρυών; see MM, VGT, see word), [in LXX: [[proverbs 30 31|Pro.30:31]]) (זַרְזִיר; BDB, Lex., 267)* ;] a cock: [[matthew 26 34|Mat.26:34]], [[mark 14 30|Mrk.14:30, 68 14:72]] [[luke 22 34|Luk.22:34, 60-61]], [[john 13 38|Jhn.13:38 18:27]].† (AS)
Ἀλεξανδρεύς, -έως, ὁ an Alexandrian: [[acts 6 9|Act.6:9 18:24]].† (AS)
Ἀλεξανδρινός (Rec. -δρῖνο; see Kühner3, II, 296), -ή, -όν, Alexan­drian: [[acts 27 6|Act.27:6 28:11]].† (AS)

Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ, Alexander 1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]] 2. A kinsman of the High Priest: [[acts 4 6|Act.4:6.]] 3. A certain Jew: [[acts 19 33|Act.19:33.]] 4. A coppersmith: [[1-timothy 1 20|1Ti.1:20.]] 5. Perh. = 4 (see Ellic. on I Ti, l.with): [[2-timothy 4 14|2Ti.4:14.]] † (AS)

Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ, Alexander 1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]] 2. A kinsman of the High Priest: [[acts 4 6|Act.4:6.]] 3. A certain Jew: [[acts 19 33|Act.19:33.]] 4. A coppersmith: [[1-timothy 1 20|1Ti.1:20.]] 5. Perh. = 4 (see Ellic. on I Ti, l.with): [[2-timothy 4 14|2Ti.4:14.]] † (AS)

Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ, Alexander 1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]] 2. A kinsman of the High Priest: [[acts 4 6|Act.4:6.]] 3. A certain Jew: [[acts 19 33|Act.19:33.]] 4. A coppersmith: [[1-timothy 1 20|1Ti.1:20.]] 5. Perh. = 4 (see Ellic. on I Ti, l.with): [[2-timothy 4 14|2Ti.4:14.]] † (AS)

Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ, Alexander 1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]] 2. A kinsman of the High Priest: [[acts 4 6|Act.4:6.]] 3. A certain Jew: [[acts 19 33|Act.19:33.]] 4. A coppersmith: [[1-timothy 1 20|1Ti.1:20.]] 5. Perh. = 4 (see Ellic. on I Ti, l.with): [[2-timothy 4 14|2Ti.4:14.]] † (AS)
ἄλευρον, -ου, τό (ἀλεύω, to grind), [in LXX for קֶמַח, [[numbers 5 15|Num.5:15]], al. ;] real: [[matthew 13 33|Mat.13:33]], [[luke 13 21|Luk.13:21]].† (AS)

ἀλήθεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀληθής), [in LXX chiefly for אֱמֶת (on which, see Cremer, 627f.), אֱמוּנָה ;] truth (see DB, iv, 818f.). 1. Objectively, "the reality lying at the basis of an appearance; the manifested, veritable essence of a matter" (Cremer, 86): [[romans 9 1|Rom.9:1]], al.; of religious truth, [[romans 1 25|Rom.1:25]], al.; esp. of Christian doctrine, [[galatians 2 5|Gal.2:5]], al.; ἀ. θεοῦ, [[romans 15 8|Rom.15:8.]] 2. Subjectively, truthfulness, truth, not merely verbal (cl.), but sincerity and integrity of character: [[john 8 44|Jhn.8:44]], 3Jo.3. 3. In phrases (MM, VGT, see word): ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας, [[mark 12 14|Mrk.12:14]], al.; ἀ. λέγειν (εἰπεῖν, λαλεῖν), [[romans 9 1|Rom.9:1]], [[2-corinthians 12 6|2Co.12:6]], [[ephesians 4 25|Eph.4:25]], al.; ἀ. ποιεῖν, [[john 3 21|Jhn.3:21]], [[1-john 1 6|1Jn.1:6]] (cf. DB, iv, 818b, ff.). (AS)

ἀληθεύω (ἀληθής), [in LXX: [[genesis 20 16|Gen.20:16]] (יָכַח) [[genesis 42 16|Gen.42:16]] (אֶמֶת), [[proverbs 21 3|Pro.21:3]] (מִשְׁפָּט), [[isaiah 44 26|Isa.44:26]] (שָׁלַם), Sir.34:4 * ;] to speak the truth (R, mg., deal truly; Field, Notes, 192): [[galatians 4 16|Gal.4:16]], [[ephesians 4 15|Eph.4:15]].† (AS)

ἀληθής, -ές (λήθω = λανθάνω, hence primarily, unconcealed, manifest; hence, actual, real), [in LXX for אֶמֶת, etc. ;] (a) of things, true, conforming to reality: [[john 4 18|Jhn.4:18 5:31-32 6:55]] (= ἀληθινός, which see) [[john 8 13|Jhn.8:13-14, 17 10:41 19:35 21:24]], [[acts 12 9|Act.12:9]], [[philippians 4 8|Php.4:8]], [[titus 1 13|Tit.1:13]], [[1-peter 5 12|1Pe.5:12]], [[2-peter 2 22|2Pe.2:22]], [[1-john 2 6|1Jn.2:6]], 3Jn.12; (b) of persons, truthful: [[matthew 22 16|Mat.22:16]], [[mark 12 14|Mrk.12:14]], [[john 3 33|Jhn.3:33 7:18 8:26]], [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4]], [[2-corinthians 6 8|2Co.6:8]].† SYN.: ἀληθινός, real, genuine, ideal, as opposite to spurious or imperfect ἀληθής, true to fact, as opposite to false, lying, denotes the actuality of a thing: ἀληθινός, its relation to the corresponding con­ception. (Cf. Tr., Syn., § viii; Cremer, 84 f., 631 Abbott, JV, 234 f.; DB, iv, 818 f.; MM, VGT, s.vv.) (AS)

ἀληθινός, -ή, -όν (ἀληθής), [in LXX for אֶמֶת ;] true, in the sense of real, ideal, genuine: [[luke 16 11|Luk.16:11]] [[john 1 9|Jhn.1:9 4:23, 37 6:32 7:28 8:16 15:1 17:3 19:35]], [[1-thessalonians 1 9|1Th.1:9]], [[hebrews 8 2|Heb.8:2 9:24 10:22]], [[1-john 2 8|1Jn.2:8]] [[john 5 20|Jn 5:20]], [[revelation 3 7|Rev.3:7, 14 6:10 15:3 16:7 19:2]]; = ἀληθής, [[revelation 19 9|Rev.19:9 21:5 22:6]] (MM, VGT, see word).† SYN.: ἀληθής, q.v (AS)
ἀλήθω (κοινή form of the Attic ἀλέω), [in LXX for טָחַן ;] to grind: [[matthew 24 41|Mat.24:41]], [[luke 17 35|Luk.17:35]].† (AS)

ἀληθῶς adv. (ἀληθής). [in LXX ([[jeremiah 28 6|Jer.28:6]], [[psalms 58 1|Psa.58:1]], al.) chiefly for אָמֵן and cogn. forms ;] truly, surely: [[matthew 14 33|Mat.14:33 26:73]] [[mark 14 70|Mrk.14:70 15:39]], [[luke 9 27|Luk.9:27 12:44 21:3]], [[john 1 48|Jhn.1:48 4:42 6:14 7:26, 40 8:31 17:8]] [[acts 12 11|Act.12:11]], [[1-thessalonians 2 13|1Th.2:13]], [[1-john 2 5|1Jn.2:5]].† (AS)

ἁλεεύς (Rec. ἁλιεύς, the older form; WH, App., 151, -έως, ὁ (ἅλς, the sea) [in LXX for דָּג, דַּוָּג ;] a fisherman: [[matthew 4 18|Mat.4:18, 19]], [[mark 1 16|Mrk.1:16, 17]], [[luke 5 2|Luk.5:2]] (AS)
ἁλιεύω (ἁλιεύς), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 16 16|Jer.16:16]] (דִּיג)* ;] to fish: [[john 21 3|Jhn.21:3]] (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἁλίζω (ἅλς), [in LXX for מָלַח ;] to salt, season with salt: [[matthew 5 13|Mat.5:13]], [[mark 9 49|Mrk.9:49]].† (AS)
ἀλίσγημα, -τος, τό (late ἀλισγέω, to pollute) pollution: [[acts 15 20|Act.15:20.]]† (AS)

ἀλλά (ἀλλ᾽ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146), adversative particle, stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. [[romans 3 31|Rom.3:31]]); 1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., [[matthew 5 15|Mat.5:15, 17]] [[mark 5 39|Mrk.5:39]], [[john 7 16|Jhn.7:16]], al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., not so much . . . as, [[mark 9 37|Mrk.9:37]], [[matthew 10 20|Mat.10:20]], [[john 12 44|Jhn.12:44]], al.; with ellipse of the negation, [[matthew 11 7|Mat.11:7-9]], [[acts 19 2|Act.19:2]], [[1-corinthians 3 6|1Co.3:6 6:11 7:7]], [[2-corinthians 7 1|2Co.7:1]], [[galatians 2 3|Gal.2:3]], al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, [[matthew 24 6|Mat.24:6]], [[1-corinthians 10 23|1Co.10:23]]; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, [[john 5 18|Jhn.5:18]], [[romans 1 32|Rom.1:32]], al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, [[mark 14 49|Mrk.14:49]], [[john 1 8|Jhn.1:8 9:3]], al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), [[matthew 20 23|Mat.20:23]], [[mark 4 22|Mrk.4:22]]. 2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: [[john 16 20|Jhn.16:20 12:27]], [[galatians 2 14|Gal.2:14]]; before commands or requests, [[acts 10 20|Act.10:20 26:16]], [[matthew 9 18|Mat.9:18]], [[mark 9 22|Mrk.9:22]], al.; to introduce an accessory idea, [[2-corinthians 7 11|2Co.7:11;]] in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, [[mark 14 29|Mrk.14:29]], [[1-corinthians 9 2|1Co.9:2]], [[2-corinthians 4 16|2Co.4:16]], [[colossians 2 5|Col.2:5]], al.; after μέν, [[acts 4 17|Act.4:17]], [[romans 14 20|Rom.14:20]], [[1-corinthians 14 17|1Co.14:17]]; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ᾽ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., [[john 16 2|Jhn.16:2;]] so with neg., ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, [[luke 23 15|Luk.23:15.]] 3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, [[luke 24 21|Luk.24:21]], [[1-corinthians 9 2|1Co.9:2]]; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, [[luke 12 51|Luk.12:51]], [[2-corinthians 1 13|2Co.1:13]]; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, [[philippians 3 8|Php.3:8]] (on this usage, see MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

ἀλλάσσω (ἄλλος), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַף, מוּר hi., etc. ;] 1. to change: [[acts 6 14|Act.6:14]], [[galatians 4 20|Gal.4:20]]. 2. to transform: [[1-corinthians 15 51|1Co.15:51-52]], [[hebrews 1 12|Heb.1:12]]. 3. to exchange: with accusative, before ἐν (= בְּ, [[psalms 106 20|Psa.106:20]]) instead of simple genitive (Bl., § 36, 8), [[romans 1 23|Rom.1:23]] (cf. ἀπ-, δι-, κατ-, ἀπο-κατ-, μετ-, συν-αλλάσσω; see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀλλαχόθεν adv. (ἀλλος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:7 * ;] = ἀλλοθεν (seeMM, VGT, see word) from another place: [[john 10 1|Jhn.10:1.]]† (AS)
ἀλληγορέω, -ῶ (ἄλλος, ἀγορεύω) to speak allegorically (Cremer, 96 ff.): [[galatians 4 24|Gal.4:24.]]† (AS)

ἁλληλουιά (Rec. ἀλληλούϊα; Heb. הָלַל יָהּ, praise the Lord), [in LXX in the titles of certain Psa (104 (105), al.), and at the end of [[psalms 150 1|Psa.150:1-6;]] also Tob.13:18, 3Ma.7:13 ;] hallelujah, alleluia: [[revelation 19 1|Rev.19:1, 3-4 19:6]].† (AS)

ἀλλήλων (genitive pl.), dative -οις, -αις, accusative -ους, -ας, -α (no nom.), recipr. pron. (ἄλλος), of one another, mutually: [[matthew 25 32|Mat.25:32]], [[mark 4 41|Mrk.4:41]], [[john 13 22|Jhn.13:22]], al. (AS)
ἀλλογενής, -ές (ἄλλος, γένος), [in LXX chiefly for זוּר, נֵכָר ;] of another race, a foreigner ( = ἀλλόφυλος; Cremer, 150; MM, VGT, see word): [[luke 17 18|Luk.17:18.]]† (AS)
ἅλλομαι [in LXX for צָלַח, דָּלַג pi., etc. ;] to leap: [[acts 3 8|Act.3:8 14:10]]; of water, to spring up, [[john 4 14|Jhn.4:14]] (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἄλλος, -η, -ο, (cf. Lat. alius, Eng. else), [in LXX for אַחֵר ,אֶחָד, etc. ;] other, another: absol., [[matthew 20 3|Mat.20:3]], al.; ἄ. δέ, [[1-corinthians 3 10|1Co.3:10 12:8]]; pl., [[mark 6 15|Mrk.6:15;]] attached to a noun, [[matthew 2 12|Mat.2:12 4:21]], al.; with art., ὁ ἄ., the other, [[matthew 5 39|Mat.5:39]], [[john 19 32|Jhn.19:32]] (Bl., §47, 8); οἱ ἄ., the others, the rest, [[john 20 25|Jhn.20:25]], [[1-corinthians 14 29|1Co.14:29]]; ἄ. πρὸς ἄλλον = πρὸς ἀλλήλους (BL, §48, 10), [[acts 2 12|Act.2:12;]] ἄλλ᾽ (i.e. ἄλλο) ἤ (Bl., §77, 13), [[luke 12 51|Luk.12:51;]] before πλήν, [[mark 12 32|Mrk.12:32;]] εἰ μή, [[john 6 22|Jhn.6:22;]] παρά with accusative, [[1-corinthians 3 11|1Co.3:11.]] SYN.: ἕτερος, which see ἄ. denotes numerical, ἕ. qualitative difference (Cremer, 89). ἄ. generally "denotes simply distinction of individuals, ἕ. involves the secondary idea of difference in kind" (see Lft., Meyer, Ramsay, on [[galatians 1 6|Gal.1:6]], 7; Tr., Syn., §xcv; BL, §51, 6; M, Pr., 79f., 246; MM, VGT, s.vv.). As to whether the distinction can be maintained in [[1-corinthians 12 8|1Co.12:8, 10]] see ICC, in l., and on [[hebrews 11 35|Heb.11:35]]f., see Westc, in l. (AS)
ἀλλοτρι-επίσκοπος (Rec. ἀλλοτριοεπ-), -ου, ὁ one who meddles in things alien to his calling: [[1-peter 4 15|1Pe.4:15]] (see ICC, in l; Deiss., BS, 224-4; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἀλλότριος, -α, -ον (ἄλλος), [in LXX for זוּר, נֵכָר, אַחֵר ;] 1. be-longing to another, not one's own (opposite to ἴδιος): [[luke 16 12|Luk.16:12]], [[romans 14 4|Rom.14:4 15:20]] (Field, Notes, 165 f.), [[2-corinthians 10 15|2Co.10:15-16]], [[1-timothy 5 22|1Ti.5:22]], [[hebrews 9 25|Heb.9:25]]. 2. foreign, strange, alien (opposite to οἰκεῖος; see MM, VGT, see word): [[matthew 17 25|Mat.17:25-26]], [[john 10 5|Jhn.10:5]], [[acts 7 6|Act.7:6]], [[hebrews 11 9|Heb.11:9, 34]].† (AS)
ἀλλόφυλος, -ον (ἄλλος, φῦλον, a tribe), [in LXX chiefly for פְּלֶשֶׁת ;] foreign, of another race (MM, VGT, see word); as opposite to a Jew, a Gentile: [[acts 10 28|Act.10:28.]]† (AS)
ἄλλως adv. (ἄλλος), otherwise: [[1-timothy 5 25|1Ti.5:25.]]† (AS)
ἀλοάω, -ῶ (ἅλως, see: ἅλων; and cf. MM, VGT, see word), [in LXX chiefly for דּוּשׁ ;] to thresh: [[1-corinthians 9 9|1Co.9:9 9:13]]; [[1-timothy 5 18|1Ti.5:18]].† (AS)

ἄ-λογος, -ον [in LXX: [[exodus 6 12|Exo.6:12]] (שָׂפָה עָרֵל), [[numbers 6 12|Num.6:12]] (נָפַל), [[job 11 12|Job.11:12]], Wis.11:15-16, 4Ma.3:1-21 * ;] 1. without reason, irrational: ζῷα, [[2-peter 2 12|2Pe.2:12]], Ju 10. 2. contrary to reason: [[acts 25 27|Act.25:27]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀλόη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: [[song-of-solomon 4 14|Sng.4:14]] א (אֲהָלִים)* ;] the aloe, aloes (the powder of a fragrant wood): [[john 19 39|Jhn.19:39.]]† (AS)
ἅλς, ἁλός, ὁ variant for ἅλας (which see): [[mark 9 49|Mrk.9:49]], Rec. WH, mg., R, mg.† (AS)
ἁλυκός, -ή, -όν (ἅλς), [in LXX for מְלַח, שִׂדִּים ;] salt: [[james 3 12|Jas.3:12.]]† (AS)
ἄλυπος, -ον (λύπη), free from grief: [[philippians 2 28|Php.2:28.]]† (AS)

ἅλυσις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX: Wis.17:17 * ;] a chain, bond: [[mark 5 3|Mrk.5:3-4]], [[luke 8 29|Luk.8:29]], [[acts 12 6|Act.12:6-7 21:33 28:20]], [[ephesians 6 20|Eph.6:20]], [[2-timothy 1 16|2Ti.1:16]], [[revelation 20 1|Rev.20:1]].† (AS)
ἀ-λυσιτελής, -ές (cf. λυσιτελέω), unprofitable: [[hebrews 13 17|Heb.13:17.]]† (AS)

Ἀλφαῖος (WH, Ἀλ-), -ου, ὁ (Aram. חַלְפַּי) Alphæus. 1. Father of Levi: [[mark 2 14|Mrk.2:14.]] 2. Father of James: [[matthew 10 3|Mat.10:3]], [[mark 3 13|Mrk.3:13]], [[luke 6 15|Luk.6:15]], [[acts 1 13|Act.1:13]].† (AS)

Ἀλφαῖος (WH, Ἀλ-), -ου, ὁ (Aram. חַלְפַּי) Alphæus. 1. Father of Levi: [[mark 2 14|Mrk.2:14.]] 2. Father of James: [[matthew 10 3|Mat.10:3]], [[mark 3 13|Mrk.3:13]], [[luke 6 15|Luk.6:15]], [[acts 1 13|Act.1:13]].† (AS)

ἅλων, -ωνος (for Attic ἅλως, -ω, see MM, VGT, see word), ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for גֹּרֶן ;] a threshing floor: [[matthew 3 12|Mat.3:12]], [[luke 3 17|Luk.3:17]] (here prob. by meton. = the grain on the threshing floor).† (AS)
ἀλώπηξ, -εκος, ἡ [in LXX for שׁוּעָל ;] a fox: [[matthew 8 20|Mat.8:20]], [[luke 9 58|Luk.9:58]]; metaphorically, of Herod, [[luke 13 32|Luk.13:32.]]† (AS)
ἅλωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἁλίσκομαι), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 50 46|Jer.50:46]] (תָּפַשׂ ni.)* ;] a taking, capture: [[2-peter 2 12|2Pe.2:12.]]† (AS)

ἅμα adv., at once (Lat. simul): [[acts 24 26|Act.24:26 27:40]], [[romans 3 12|Rom.3:12]] (one and all = יַחַד, [[psalms 14 3|Psa.14:3]]), [[colossians 4 3|Col.4:3]], [[1-timothy 5 13|1Ti.5:13]], Phm 22; before σύν, [[1-thessalonians 4 17|1Th.4:17 5:10]]; as prep. with dative, together with: [[matthew 13 29|Mat.13:29]] (see MM, VGT, see word); also, with adv., ἅ. πρωΐ (cl., ἅ. ἕω, etc.), early in the morning: [[matthew 20 1|Mat.20:1.]]† (AS)
ἀμαθής, -ές (μανθάνω), [in Sm.: [[psalms 49 11|Psa.49:11]] * ;] unlearned, ignorant: [[2-peter 3 16|2Pe.3:16]] (on the rareness of this word, see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀμαράντινος, -ον (ἀμάραντος), of amaranth (Inscr.); hence un­fading: [[1-peter 5 4|1Pe.5:4.]]† (AS)
ἀμάραντος, -ον (μαραίνομαι), [in LXX: Wis.6:12 (σοφία)* ;] un­fading (whence ὁ ἀ., the amaranth, an unfading flower): [[1-peter 1 4|1Pe.1:4]] (cf. MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἁμαρτάνω (present formed from aor. ἁμαρτεῖν), [in LXX for חָטָא, also for אָשַׁם, רָשַׁע, etc. ;] 1. to miss the mark (Hom., Æsch., al.), hence metaphorically (Hom., al.), to err, do wrong 2. In LXX and NT, to violate God's law, to sin (for non-Christian exx., see MM, VGT, see word): absol., [[matthew 18 25|Mat.18:25 27:4]], [[luke 17 3|Luk.17:3]], [[john 5 14|Jhn.5:14 8:11 9:2-3]] [[romans 2 12|Rom.2:12 3:23 5:12, 14 5:16 6:15]], [[1-corinthians 7 28|1Co.7:28 7:36 15:34]], [[ephesians 4 26|Eph.4:26]], [[1-timothy 5 20|1Ti.5:20]], [[titus 3 11|Tit.3:11]], [[hebrews 3 17|Heb.3:17 10:26]], [[1-peter 2 20|1Pe.2:20]], [[2-peter 2 4|2Pe.2:4 2:4]] [[1-john 1 10|1Jn.1:10]] [[john 2 1|Jn 2:1]] [[john 3 6|Jn 3:6-9]] [[john 5 18|Jn 5:18]]; with cogn. accusative, ἁ. ἁμαρτίαν (cf. [[exodus 32 30|Exo.32:30]], חֲטָאָה חָטָא), [[1-john 5 16|1Jn.5:16;]] before εἰς, [[matthew 18 21|Mat.18:21]], [[luke 15 18|Luk.15:18, 21 17:4]], [[acts 25 8|Act.25:8]] (καίσαρα). [[1-corinthians 6 18|1Co.6:18 8:12]] (Field, Notes, 173); ἐνώπιον, [[luke 15 18|Luk.15:18, 21]]; πρὸς θάνατον (cf. [[numbers 18 22|Num.18:22]], מוּת חֵטְא), [[1-john 5 16|1Jn.5:16]] (Cremer, 98, 633).† (AS)

ἁμάρτημα, -τος, τό (ἁμαρτεῖν, see supr.), [in LXX for חַטָּאָה, עָוֺן etc. ;] an act of disobedience to divine law (Lft., Notes, 273), a sinful deed, a sin: [[mark 3 28|Mrk.3:28-29]], [[romans 3 25|Rom.3:25]], [[1-corinthians 6 18|1Co.6:18]], [[2-peter 1 9|2Pe.1:9]], WH, mg.; αἰώνιωv ἀ. (DCG, i, 788a), [[mark 3 29|Mrk.3:29]] (for exx. from π., see MM, VGT, see word).† SYN.: ἀγνόημα, ἁμαρτία, ἀνομία, ἀσέβεια, ἥττημα, παράβασις, παρακοή, παρανομία, παράπτωμα (ν. Cremer, 100; Tr., Syn., § lxvi; DB, iv, 532; DCG, l.with; Westc, Eph., 165 f.) (AS)

ἁμαρτία, -ας, ἡ (ἁμαρτάνω, which see), [in LXX chiefly for חַטָּאת and cogn. forms, also for פֶּשַׁע ,עָוֹן, etc. ;] prop. a missing the mark; in cl. (see reff. to CR in MM, VGT, see word); (a) guilt, sin (Plat., Arist., al.); (b) more freq., from Æsch. down, a fault, failure. In NT (as LXX) always in ethical sense; 1. as a principle and quality of action, = τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν, a sinning, sin: [[romans 5 12|Rom.5:12, 13 20]]; ὑφ᾽ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι, [[romans 3 9|Rom.3:9;]] ἐπιμένειν, [[romans 6 1|Rom.6:1;]] ἀποθνήσκειν, νεκρὸν εἶναι τῇ ἁ., [[romans 6 2|Rom.6:2, 11]]; τὴν ἀ. γινώσκειν, [[romans 7 7|Rom.7:7;]] σῶμα τῆς ἁ., [[romans 6 6|Rom.6:6;]] ἀπάτη τῆς ἁ., [[hebrews 3 13|Heb.3:13;]] personified as a ruling principle, ἁ. βασιλεύει, κυριεύει, etc., [[romans 5 21|Rom.5:21]] 6:12, 14 7:17, 20; δουλεύειν, [[romans 6 6|Rom.6:6;]] δοῦλος τῆς ἁ., ib. 17; νόμος τῆς ἁ., [[romans 7 23|Rom.7:23 8:2]]; δύναμις τῆς ἁ., [[1-corinthians 15 56|1Co.15:56]] (cf. [[genesis 4 7|Gen.4:7]]). 2. As a generic term (disting. fr. the specific terms ἁμάρτημα, which see, etc.) for concrete wrongdoing, violation of the divine law, sin: [[john 8 46|Jhn.8:46]], [[james 1 15|Jas.1:15]], al.; ποιεῖν (τὴν) ἁ., [[john 8 34|Jhn.8:34]], [[2-corinthians 11 7|2Co.11:7]], [[1-john 3 8|1Jn.3:8]]; εἴχειν ἁ., [[john 9 41|Jhn.9:41 15:22, 24 19:11]], [[1-john 1 8|1Jn.1:8]]; in pl. ἁμαρτίαι, sin in the aggregate, [[1-thessalonians 2 16|1Th.2:16]] (see Milligan, in l.); ποιεῖν ἁμαρτίας, [[james 5 15|Jas.5:15;]] πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν, [[james 5 20|Jas.5:20]], 1Pe.4:8; ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν, [[matthew 26 28|Mat.26:28]], [[mark 1 4|Mrk.1:4]], al.; ἐν ἁμαρτίαις εἶναι, [[1-corinthians 15 17|1Co.15:17;]] collectively, αἴρειν τὴν ἁ. τ. κόσμου, [[john 1 29|Jhn.1:29;]] ἀποθνήσκειν ἐν τῇ ἁ., [[john 8 21|Jhn.8:21.]] 3. = ἁμάρτημα, a sinful deed, a sin: [[matthew 12 31|Mat.12:31]], [[acts 7 60|Act.7:60]], [[1-john 5 16|1Jn.5:16]]. SYN.: see: ἁμάρτημα. (AS)
ἀμάρτυρος, -ον (μάρτυς), without witness: [[acts 14 17|Act.14:17.]]† (AS)

ἁμαρτωλός, -όν (ἁμαρτάνω), [in LXX chiefly for רָשָׁע ;] sinful, a sinner: of all men, [[1-timothy 1 15|1Ti.1:15;]] of those especially wicked, [[1-timothy 1 9|1Ti.1:9]], [[1-peter 4 18|1Pe.4:18]]; p1., [[matthew 9 10|Mat.9:10-13 11:19 26:45]], al. (see MM, VGT, see word; Cremer, 102, 634) (AS)

ἄμαχος, -ον (μάχη); 1. invincible (frequently in cl.). 2. abstaining from fighting, non-combatant (Xen.). Metaphorical (cf. MM, VGT, see word), not contentious: [[1-timothy 3 3|1Ti.3:3]], [[titus 3 2|Tit.3:2]].† (AS)
ἀμάω, -ῶ (in cl. chiefly poët.), to reap: [[james 5 4|Jas.5:4.]]† (AS)

ἀμέθυστος, -ου, ἡ (accusative to Plut., ἀ- μεθύω, being regarded as an antidote against drunkenness) [in LXX: [[exodus 28 19|Exo.28:19 36:19 39:12]] [[ezekiel 28 13|Eze.28:13]] * ;] amethyst, a purple quartz: [[revelation 21 20|Rev.21:20.]]† (AS)

ἀμελέω, -ῶ (μέλει), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 4 17|Jer.4:17]] (מָרָה) [[jeremiah 31 32|Jer.31:32]] (בַּעַל), Wis.3:10, 2Ma.4:14 * ;] (a) absol., to be careless, not to care: [[matthew 22 5|Mat.22:5;]] (b) with genitive, to be careless of, to neglect: [[1-timothy 4 14|1Ti.4:14]], [[hebrews 2 3|Heb.2:3 8:9]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἄ-μεμπτος, -ον (μέμφομσι), [in LXX chiefly for תָּם ;] blameless, free from fault (in π. of a marriage-contract; M, Th., I, 3:13; cf. MM, VGT, see word): [[luke 1 6|Luk.1:6]], [[philippians 2 15|Php.2:15 3:6]], [[1-thessalonians 3 13|1Th.3:13]] (WH, mg., -ως) [[hebrews 8 7|Heb.8:7.]]† SYN.: ἄμωμος, ἀνέγκλητος, ἀνεπίλημπτος, which see (Tr., Syn., § ciii) (AS)
ἀ-μέμπτως, adv. (ἄμεμπτος), [in LXX: [[esther 3 13|Est.3:13]] * ;] blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, see word -ος): [[1-thessalonians 2 10|1Th.2:10 3:13]] WH mg., 5:23.† (AS)
ἀμέριμνος, -ον (μέριμνα), [in LXX: Wis.6:15 7:23 * ;] free from anxiety or care: [[matthew 28 14|Mat.28:14]], [[1-corinthians 7 32|1Co.7:32]] (for exx., see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀ-μετάθετος, -ον (μετατίθημι), [in LXX: 3Ma.5:1 3Mac 5:12 * ;] immutable: [[hebrews 6 18|Heb.6:18;]] as subat., τὸ ἀ., immutability, [[hebrews 6 17|Heb.6:17]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀ-μετα-κίνητος, -ον (μετακινέω), immovable, firm: [[1-corinthians 15 58|1Co.15:58.]]† (AS)
ἀ-μεταμέλητος, -ον (μεταμέλομαι), not repented of, unregretted: [[romans 11 29|Rom.11:29]], [[2-corinthians 7 10|2Co.7:10]].† (AS)
ἀμετανόητος, -ον (μετανοέω) 1. impenitent: [[romans 2 5|Rom.2:5]] 2. = ἀμεταμέλητος (π., Philo, al.; see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἄμετρος, -ον (μέτρον), without measure: adverbially, εἰς τὰ ἄ., excessively, [[2-corinthians 10 13|2Co.10:13 10:15]]† (AS)

ἀμήν, indecl. (Heb. אָמֵן, verbal adj. fr. אמן, to prop. ni., be firm), [in LXX: [[1-chronicles 16 36|1Ch.16:36]], I [[esther 9 46|Est.9:46]], [[nehemiah 5 13|Neh.5:13 8:6]], Tob.8:8 14:15, 3Ma.7:23, 4Ma.18:24 (elsewhere ''א is rendered ἀληθινός, [[isaiah 65 16|Isa.65:16;]] ἀληθῶς, [[jeremiah 28 6|Je 35 (28):6]]; γένοιτο, [[numbers 5 22|Num.5:22]], [[deuteronomy 27 15|Deu.27:15]]ff., [[1-kings 1 36|3Ki.1:36]], Psa.40 (41):13 71 (72):19 105 (106):48, [[jeremiah 11 5|Jer.11:5]])*.] 1. As adj. (cf. Is, l.with), ὁ ἀ., [[revelation 3 14|Rev.3:14.]] 2. As adv., (a) in solemn assent to the statements or prayers of another (Nu, Ne, etc., ll. with): ὁ ἀ., [[1-corinthians 14 16|1Co.14:16;]] (b) similarly, at the end of one's own prayer or ascription of praise: [[romans 1 25|Rom.1:25 15:33]], [[galatians 1 5|Gal.1:5]], [[1-timothy 1 17|1Ti.1:17]]; (with) in the Gospels, exclusively, introducing solemn statements of our Lord, truly, verily: [[matthew 5 18|Mat.5:18, 26]] [[mark 3 28|Mrk.3:28]] (see Swete, in l.), [[luke 4 24|Luk.4:24]], al.; ἀ. ἀ., always in [[john 1 52|Jhn.1:52 3:3 5:19]], al.; τὸ ναί, καὶ . . . τὸ ἀ., [[2-corinthians 1 20|2Co.1:20]] (on usage in π., see MM, VGT, see word). (AS)
ἀμήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ, ἡ (μήτηρ), without a mother (frequently in Gk. writers of the gods): ἀπάτωρ ἀ. of one without recorded genealogy, [[hebrews 7 3|Heb.7:3]] (cf. MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

ἀ-μίαντος, -ον (μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.3:13 4:2 8:20, 2Ma.14:36 2Mac 15:34 * ;] undefiled, free from contamination (in π., of αἰθήρ; MM, VGT, see word): [[hebrews 7 26|Heb.7:26 13:4]], [[1-peter 1 4|1Pe.1:4]], [[james 1 27|Jas.1:27]].† SYN.: ἄμωμος, ἄσπιλος (Cremer, 784) (AS)
Ἀμιναδάβ, ὁ indecl. (Heb עַמִּינָדָב), Amminadab: [[matthew 1 4|Mat.1:4]], [[luke 3 33|Luk.3:33]] (WH om.).† (AS)

ἄμμος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חוֹל ;] sand, sandy ground: [[matthew 7 26|Mat.7:26]], [[romans 9 27|Rom.9:27]], [[hebrews 11 12|Heb.11:12]], [[revelation 18 1|Rev.18:1]], [[revelation 20 8|Rev.20:8]].† (AS)

ἀμνός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for כֶּבֶשׂ ;] a lamb: figuratively, of Christ (DCG, ii, 620b), [[john 1 29|Jhn.1:29, 36]], [[acts 8 32|Act.8:32]]" (LXX), [[1-peter 1 19|1Pe.1:19]] (cf. ἀρνίον; Cremer, 102, 635).† (AS)
ἀμοιβή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀμείβομαι, to repay); [in Aq., Sm.: [[proverbs 12 14|Pro.12:14]], al. ;] requital, recompense: [[1-timothy 5 4|1Ti.5:4]] (for illustration from τ.. see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἄμπελος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for גֶּפֶן ;] vine: [[matthew 26 29|Mat.26:29]], [[mark 14 25|Mrk.14:25]], [[luke 22 18|Luk.22:18]] [[james 3 12|Jas.3:12]]; figuratively, of Christ, [[john 15 1|Jhn.15:1, 4-5]]; of his enemies (on the usage here, see MM, VGT, see word): [[revelation 14 18|Rev.14:18-19.]]† (AS)
ἀμπελουργός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for כֹּרֵם ;] a vine dresser: [[luke 13 7|Luk.13:7.]]† (AS)

ἀμπελών, -ῶνος, ὁ (ἄμπελος), [in LXX for כֶּרֶם ;] a vineyard: [[matthew 20 1|Mat.20:1]] ff. [[matthew 21 28|Mat.21:28]] ff, [[luke 13 6|Luk.13:6 20:9]] ff., [[1-corinthians 9 7|1Co.9:7]]. Æschin., 49, 13; Diod., al.; see MM, VGT, see word; LS, see word ἀμπελουργεῖον.) (AS)
Ἀμπλιᾶτος (T, -ίατος; Rec. Ἀμπλιᾶς; see MM, VGT, 5.see), -ου, ὁ Ampliatus: [[romans 1 6|Rom.1:6 8:8]].† (AS)

ἀμύνω [in LXX (mid.): [[joshua 10 13|Jos.10:13]] (נָקַם), נָקַם), [[psalms 118 10|Psa.118:10-12]] מוּל hi.), [[isaiah 59 16|Isa.59:16]] (יָשַׁע hi.), Wis.11:3, al. ;] to ward off, etc. Mid. (a) to defend oneself against; (b) to requite; (with) = act., to defend, assist (Isa, l.with): with accusative of person(s), [[acts 7 24|Act.7:24]] (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀμφίβληστρον, -ου, τό (ἀμφιβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;] something thrown around, as a garment; spec., a casting-net: [[matthew 4 18|Mat.4:18.]]† (AS)
ἀμφιέννυμι (ἕννυμι, to clothe), to clothe: [[matthew 6 30|Mat.6:30 11:8]], [[luke 7 25|Luk.7:25]] (cf. ἀμφιάζω).† (AS)
Ἀμφίπολις, -εως, ἡ Amphipolis, in Macedonia, so called because the river Strymon flowed around it: [[acts 17 1|Act.17:1.]]† (AS)

ἄμφοδον, -ου, το (ἀμφί ὁδός), [in LXX for אַרְמוֹן ([[jeremiah 17 27|Jer.17:27 30:10 49:27]])* ;] prop., a road around anything (RV, the open street): [[mark 11 4|Mrk.11:4]], [[acts 19 28|Act.19:28]], WH, mg.† (AS)
ἀμφότεροι, -αι, -α (replaces ἄμφω in κοινή, V. M, Pr., 57; used of more than two, Pr., 80; MM, VGT, see word), both of two: [[matthew 9 17|Mat.9:17]], al. (AS)
ἀ-μώμητος, -ου (μωμάομαι), blameless: [[2-peter 3 14|2Pe.3:14.]]† SYN.: ἄμεμπτος (which see), ἀνέγκλητος, ἀνεπίλημπτος (AS)

ἄ-μωμος, -ον (μῶμος, which see), [in LXX chiefly for תָּמִים ]; of sacrificial victims, without blemish: of Christ, [[hebrews 9 14|Heb.9:14]], [[1-peter 1 19|1Pe.1:19]]; etbically, unblemished, faultless: [[ephesians 1 4|Eph.1:4 5:27]], [[philippians 2 15|Php.2:15]], [[colossians 1 22|Col.1:22]], Ju 24, [[revelation 14 5|Rev.14:5]] (Cremer, 425, 788; MM, VGT, see word).† SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄσπιλος (AS)
